items.evidence: The acceptance test 'non-finite call-fold equity throws RangeError' passes. It loops over all 4 call-fold pairings x both fields x NaN/Infinity/-Infinity/undefined and asserts RangeError with the exact message. Error and TypeError class mutants and an equityPct-guard-removed mutant all make it fail. Holdout check passed: for every pairing and field, NaN/±Infinity/undefined/null and a fully absent key all throw an error whose constructor is exactly RangeError, with the message '<field> must be a finite number, got <String(v)>'. When both fields are bad, equityPct is reported first. Finite extremes (0/0, ±1e9) still grade, so there is no range check.

The acceptance test 'non-finite calling-range equity throws RangeError' passes. It covers 4 aggression pairings x NaN/±Infinity with an exact RangeError, and undefined/null giving minor/aggression-no-range/null. An aggression-guard-removed mutant makes it fail. Holdout check passed: exact RangeError class and message for each pairing. undefined, null and an absent key give aggression-no-range with marginPts null, even when equityPct and requiredEquityPct are NaN. Finite 65 gives major/aggression-margin/15 with NaN call-fold fields, and 45 gives minor.

The acceptance test 'unused non-finite numbers do not throw' passes. It asserts the match case on all-NaN input, correct/alternative, and major/call-fold-margin/10 with NaN calling-range equity. Holdout check passed: for all 5 actions, all-non-finite input with a matching user action gives correct/match. The alternative case gives correct/alternative. rec fold vs user call at 30/40 with NaN calling-range gives major/10. An impossible pairing with non-finite numbers still throws the existing 'fold and check cannot both be legal' error.

The acceptance test 'a -15 wrong-way margin is Minor' passes for all 4 call-fold pairings, asserting minor/call-fold-margin/-15. A Math.abs(equity - required) mutant makes it fail. Holdout check passed: -15, -0.1 (39.9 or 40.1 vs 40), -40 (0 vs 40) and -60 (100 vs 40) are all minor with the correct negative marginPts for every pairing.

In tests/advice/grade.test.ts the test is now named 'exactly 10 points is Major whether float subtraction is exact (26.7-16.7) or falls short (16.4-6.4)', and it passes. The diff from base renames that one test and adds a single line, expect(26.7 - 16.7).toBe(10). The two Major/10 assertions and expect(16.4 - 6.4).toBeLessThan(10) remain, and nothing else in the file changed (numstat +2/-1).

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected: the spec says the all-NaN matching-action case returns Correct. Actual: the code does return correct/match, but the acceptance test only asserts ruleId 'match' for that case and not grade 'correct'. A regression that changed the grade on a match would not be caught by this test.
